audio_caption: The audio clip begins with dramatic orchestral music, conveying a sense of grandeur or importance. Then a calm and measured male speaker introduces himself, along with a co-worker at The League of Women Voters in Portland. He mentions the video is a voter's guide in conjunction with Metro East Community Media, explaining the clip's purpose to converse with candidates in the May 2020 primary election. He introduces Keith Wilson, a candidate for the Portland City Council, and then asks him to tell us about himself and why he's running for the position. Keith responds, expressing gratitude and acknowledging the current crisis, offering best wishes to everyone. He is confident that we will get through this together and states his commitment to do his part for Portland.

The clip starts with a male speaker introducing himself, mentioning he was "born and raised here in Portland," giving details about his family, education at Roosevelt High School and Oregon State, and his work history including traveling overseas and returning to join his father's business. His tone is conversational and informative. He currently works in transportation as "the President of Titan Freight Systems." He also describes his wife as "an early childhood special education teacher," his daughter, and his son. The speaker then offers more about his focus.

One man speaks in an informative tone. He mentions the four key tenets of his plan: inability to maintain cleanliness, homelessness, and climate crisis. He describes himself as a transportation manager, and suggests he has solutions for all four issues, particularly related to greener technologies.

The audio begins with a male speaker discussing issues such as an "affordable housing crisis", adding that even people who have lived in or built the city "struggle to live" there. He states plans to address this and that these issues are his reasons for running for Portland City Council. The audio concludes.

A male speaker began a discussion by acknowledging the pandemic as a major challenge, then asked about potential repercussions for city government, suggesting that city council members should address "very big issues." Another male speaker responded with a clarification that they focus specifically on the pandemic.

The clip features a male speaker discussing their small business stabilization fund and the need for an "all hands on deck" approach, emphasizing the importance of taking care of their core staff and workforce and investing in it. His tone is serious and focused as he expresses a fear of recession and the need to focus on their workforce as an opportunity.

The clip features a single male speaker discussing his educational experience, specifically mentioning "Portland Community College" and how he "paid for my college". He describes a lack of opportunity in high school, attending Portland Community, and putting himself through school. The speaker urges listeners to "retrain" and view the current "crisis" as both "danger" and "opportunity". He concludes by encouraging turning the "crisis" into an "opportunity". The speaker sounds motivational and passionate.

The audio clip features a male speaker discussing the need for government support to retrain the workforce, emphasizing the importance of city resources to help businesses survive during a recession. His tone is concerned but hopeful. Following this, the audio transitions to another male speaker who responds with an "Okay".

The audio begins with a male speaker introducing the topic of city government and its structure. He mentions city council members managing various bureaus. He then poses a question about which bureaus the person would be interested in managing if they served on the city council. The other speaker agrees with the statement and does not speak further.

The clip begins with a male speaker stating "Yes, in fact, one of the main reasons I'm running for position number four is that current commissioner holds Portland Bureau of Transportation". He mentions having a master's degree in transportation and finance and having run a complex transportation organization for twenty years. The speaker notes he knows "all of the facets of running a trucking company, using road, road taxes". He believes he is a "perfect fit", and the "commission and PBOT works perfect".

A male speaker discusses the current state of city government and how it could be improved. He cites a specific example and suggests hiring a city manager with advanced management techniques. His tone is concerned and professional.

One male speaker describes their role as a council person and legislator who focuses on "developing the best policy," using benchmarking and working with the city manager to execute plans and hold bureaus accountable, stating that Portland has nothing to hold it back if well-managed, delivered in a confident and optimistic tone. Following this a speaker says "very good".

The audio clip begins with a male speaker asking another individual, named Keith, if he has time for a question. He proceeds to inquire generally about the police-community relations, the use of deadly force, and officer accountability in the city's law enforcement. The speaker's tone is inquisitive and conversational.

The audio clip features a single male speaker expressing a somber sentiment about a heartbreaking situation, potentially related to homeless individuals or mental health issues. He references a website, "Keith for portland.com", where he highlights seven platform items addressing mental illness and homelessness.

The audio features a male speaker discussing the importance of accountability and mentions a community-engaged policing program. He suggests transitioning the program from a temporary commission to a full-time operation, giving them the power to hold individuals accountable and research transgressions thoroughly. His tone is assertive and focused. He differentiates the program from the citizen review committee, advocating for a permanent body within the city structure.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker advocating for an "oversight program" to ensure accountability and support both the police and the public. He emphasizes the importance of collaboration to make Portland safer. His tone is serious and determined.

The audio begins with a cordial greeting and thanks, followed by a male speaker discussing a "voter's guide" and an upcoming "primary election." He encourages viewers to be informed and exercise their right to vote. The audio concludes with dramatic, cinematic-style music featuring orchestral instruments and a suspenseful tone.
